from.place: Tag 0658 proof: pseudo-coherence supplies a bounded-above finite-projective model, and the truncation argument makes it bounded under finite Tor dimension

title: Pseudo-coherent complexes of finite Tor dimension over a ring are perfect
statement: Let R be a ring and let C be an object of the derived category D(R) [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume C is pseudo-coherent, meaning that it admits a quasi-isomorphism from a bounded-above complex of finitely generated projective R-modules. Assume also that C has finite Tor dimension: there are integers a <= b such that H^i(C tensor_R^L M) = 0 for every R-module M and every i outside [a,b]. Then C is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective R-modules, hence is perfect in the affine sense of [def-pc-perfect-complex].

proof.text: Taking $M=R$ in the amplitude hypothesis gives $H^i(C)=0$ for $i>b$. Apply [lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-bounded-finite-free-model] to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to C$ from a complex of finitely generated free $R$-modules with $P^i=0$ for $i>b$. Derived tensor products are invariant under quasi-isomorphism, so $H^i(P^\bullet\otimes^{\mathbf L}_R M)=0$ for every $R$-module $M$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$; in particular ($M=R$) $H^i(P^\bullet)=0$ for $i<a$. Since $P^\bullet$ is a bounded-above complex of flat modules, it is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat] (applied to the one-point ringed space with ring $R$), so $P^\bullet\otimes^{\mathbf L}_R M$ is computed by the ordinary total tensor complex $P^\bullet\otimes_R M$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.2 (Tag 0658), definition of pseudo-coherence and first reduction

proof.text: Set $E^\bullet=\tau_{\ge a}P^\bullet$: the complex with $E^i=P^i$ for $i>a$, $E^a=\operatorname{coker}(d^{a-1}\colon P^{a-1}\to P^a)$ and $E^i=0$ for $i<a$, with the canonical surjective map of complexes $P^\bullet\to E^\bullet$. Because $P^i=0$ for $i>b$, $E^\bullet$ is bounded, and all its terms except $E^a$ are finitely generated free; $E^a$ is finitely presented, being the cokernel of a map $P^{a-1}\to P^a$ between finite free modules.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.2 (Tag 0658), truncation argument in the proof

proof.text: By Step 1, $H^i(P^\bullet)=0$ for $i<a$, so $\cdots\to P^{a-2}\to P^{a-1}\to P^a\to E^a\to0$ is a resolution of $E^a$ by free modules. Hence for every $R$-module $M$, $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(E^a,M)$ is the homology at $P^{a-1}\otimes_R M$ of $P^{a-2}\otimes_R M\to P^{a-1}\otimes_R M\to P^a\otimes_R M$, which is $H^{a-1}(P^\bullet\otimes_R M)=H^{a-1}(P^\bullet\otimes^{\mathbf L}_R M)=0$ by Step 1, since $a-1\notin[a,b]$. Thus $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(E^a,M)=0$ for every $M$, i.e. $E^a$ is flat (More on Algebra, Lemma 15.68.2, used in Tag 0658). Since $E^a$ is also finitely presented (Step 2), [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective] makes it a finite projective $R$-module.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.2 (Tag 0658), truncation and Tor-dimension-zero argument

proof.text: The canonical map $P^\bullet\to E^\bullet=\tau_{\ge a}P^\bullet$ induces isomorphisms on $H^i$ for $i\ge a$ by construction, and both sides have $H^i=0$ for $i<a$ (for $P^\bullet$ by Step 1); hence it is a quasi-isomorphism. With Step 3, every term of $E^\bullet$ is a finitely generated projective $R$-module, so $C\cong P^\bullet\cong E^\bullet$ in $D(R)$ with $E^\bullet$ a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.2 (Tag 0658), conclusion of the truncation argument

proof.text: A bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules is perfect in the affine sense, by the strictly-perfect clause of [def-pc-perfect-complex] on $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
